text:
carla: quick design pass — invoices table: the token-quantity pill (1.2k) next to the sparkline reads heavier than the chart. Feels like it steals the eye from the trend we want to emphasize. Screenshot: https://redwood.mock/snap/INV-pt1.png

ben: yep, noticed that too. also the pill overlaps the rightmost point at narrow widths.

mia: agree on visual weight. two quick options i sketched: 1) micro badge (icon + condensed number) to the far right, 2) hide badge under hover / row details and keep sparkline primary. which do we want to prototype?

raj: i like option 1 for glanceability but we need to keep token units clear (k vs tokens). copy/aria: badge should read like "1,200 tokens" for screen readers.

zoe: accessibility nit — sparkline needs a text alternative: "usage trend, up 12% vs prev period". If we hide the badge on hover, keyboard users won't discover it unless there's a focus target. we should avoid hover-only reveal.

carla: good call. what about making the badge visually lighter (60% opacity) and moving it to the right, but keep a concise ARIA label and a visible focus target? that preserves glanceable info without competing with chart.

ben: lightweight badge + keyboard focus target sounds pragmatic. we can also add a tooltip with exact breakdown for decimals and units: `1,234 tokens (3.4k weighted)` so human readers get detail on hover/focus.

mia: UX copy tweak: change column heading from "Tokens" to "Token count (USD est.)" ? or split into two columns? i worry adding the parenthetical bloats layout. maybe keep heading as "Tokens" and add an inline micro copy under hover that says "est. $X".

raj: prefer keep columns narrow. micro tooltip for USD est is fine. important: currency formatting should be locale-aware.

zoe: accessibility checklist: 1) badge gets aria-describedby pointing to tooltip text, 2) sparkline has aria-hidden=false with a descriptive aria-label, 3) keyboard focus order: row -> badge -> actions.

carla: implementation constraints: eng-runtime asked that we avoid adding extra DOM nodes per row (perf at 1000+ rows). so we need a solution that uses existing elements where possible (e.g., repurpose the timestamp container to host the badge).

ben: ok — engineering suggestion: render badge as part of the existing right-aligned meta container; show tooltip content via a single shared portal element to avoid per-row DOM bloat.

mia: i'll mock two variants today: (A) right-aligned low-contrast badge + shared tooltip, (B) badge hidden behind a small chevron that expands row details (explicit affordance). will post prototypes by EOD.

carla: decision for now: prototype both A+B, run a quick 5-person hallway test (PMs + support rep) next week, and pick A if we can meet keyboard discoverability without hover-only behavior.

design-bot: checklist created: [prototype A, prototype B, a11y QA, perf review with eng-runtime, small usability test]. tagging @ben @mia @raj for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
